analysis.investment_thesis: CreditAccess Grameen's net profit cratered 63% from ₹1,446 Cr (FY24) to ₹531 Cr (FY25) as the MFI sector crisis — over-indebtedness, collection failures, and RBI scrutiny — unwound a 3-year lending boom; the forward P/E of 13.65x vs trailing 41.8x tells you the market is pricing further pain, not recovery. Until asset quality stabilizes and ROE recovers toward 18–20%, this is a turnaround bet, not a compounder.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 66.28% (CreditAccess India BV) provides strong parent backing and governance; DII ownership of 13.23% shows institutional conviction at these levels
Revenue CAGR of 28.4% over 6 years (₹1,282 Cr → ₹5,752 Cr) demonstrates genuine loan book expansion into deeply underpenetrated rural women borrower segment
Forward P/E of 13.65x implies significant mean-reversion potential if MFI sector credit costs normalize in FY26–27
key_risks: PAT collapsed 63% YoY in FY25 (₹1,446 → ₹531 Cr) — this is a sector credit-crisis event, not a temporary blip; provisions are likely to remain elevated
OCF negative in 4 of 5 years (standard for MFIs but -₹4,734 Cr in FY24 reflects aggressive disbursement that is now souring) — the loan book quality is the only asset that matters
D/E of 2.81x is appropriate for NBFC structure but leaves no buffer if asset quality deteriorates further; total debt of ₹20,446 Cr vs equity ₹7,164 Cr
red_flags: ROE collapsed to 7.86% — below cost of equity for a leveraged NBFC; wealth destruction, not creation, in FY25
Market cap ₹20,251 Cr — 10x outside Kedia's ideal universe; MFI sector stress is well-publicized, meaning no information edge
Finance costs compounding at 29.4% CAGR (₹417 Cr → ₹1,955 Cr) while net profit CAGR is only 8.7% over the same period — the borrowing cost flywheel is dangerous in a stressed credit environment
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CreditAccess is the largest pure-play MFI in India by AUM, with strong rural distribution and a parent (CreditAccess India BV) that brings global microfinance expertise. The structural case for financial inclusion in rural India is real — this is exactly the kind of large, underpenetrated TAM that Kedia loves. However, the MFI sector has experienced a systemic credit event in FY25: multiple NBFCs aggressively cross-sold to the same borrower pools, and collection efficiency has fallen sharply across the industry.

The numbers confirm the stress: PAT down 63%, ROE at 7.86%, and OCF turning positive only in FY25 (after 4 consecutive negative years). The forward P/E of 13.65x suggests earnings could normalize to ₹1,400+ Cr — but that recovery is conditional on NPA stabilization that hasn't been demonstrated yet. At ₹20,251 Cr market cap, you are paying to hope. Kedia would wait for actual NPA trends to turn before considering this, and even then the market cap is 10–20x his preferred entry size.
